The club built
by its community

Not a chain. Not a franchise. A charity gym at the heart of Dunoon, run by volunteers for the town’s young people and adults.

Coached pad work, bag work and sparring — every session led by qualified volunteer coaches.

Dunoon Amateur Boxing Club is a registered charity with one simple purpose: to give the people of Cowal a place to box, get fit and grow in confidence.

The club became a registered charity in August 2015 and went on to build its own purpose-built community sports centre in the grounds of Dunoon Stadium, opened in 2019 — a home the whole town helped make happen.

It is run entirely on a not-for-profit basis: trustees and committee members give their time voluntarily, and every penny goes back into the gym, the young boxers and the community. It is the only boxing club in Argyll.

Club boxers compete in Boxing Scotland championships — including the National Championships at Ravenscraig — and the club puts on boxing shows at the Queens Hall, Dunoon, so the town can cheer on its own.

Train with us

Four ways in through the ropes — whatever your age, whatever your starting point. No experience needed, ever.

01 / JUNIORS

Children’s Boxing

Young people · all abilities

Confidence, discipline and fitness through real boxing skills — footwork, pads and bags, coached safely and patiently. The club’s young boxers are the heart of everything it does.

First step into boxing
02 / ADULTS

Adult Boxing

Fitness or competition

Train for fitness, for fun, or for the amateur squad. Bag work, pad work, sparring and conditioning with coaches who know your name and push you properly.

Fitness · Squad
“Everyone should be able to box and take part.”
03 / WOMEN

Female-Only Classes

Women & girls · all levels

Dedicated women’s sessions added to meet demand — a safe, supportive space to learn boxing, get strong and belong. Women now coach, officiate and fight at the club too.

Safe · Supportive
04 / CONDITIONING

Strength & Fitness

Build the engine

Strength and conditioning that backs up the boxing — the graft that turns good technique into real fitness, resilience and results in the ring.

Stronger every week
Evening sessions at Dunoon Stadium. Days and times are posted each week on the club’s Facebook and Instagram pages, and membership details are available by email — just ask the club.
Boxing Scotland · National Championships

Dunoon’s
history-maker

In just a short time, Dani Bancks became the club’s first female boxer, its first female champion and its first Box Cup champion — then earned a call-up to the Scotland squad for the Four Nations Championships. She trains under head coach Jordan, right here in Dunoon.

03 — Join the club

Your first step through the ropes starts with a message.

No experience needed. No pressure. Just tell the club who you are and what you’d like to try — children’s boxing, adult training, or a female-only class — and they’ll tell you when to come down to Dunoon Stadium.
